headingOrder_review_HEADING_ORDER_SKIPPE: Find the heading the report names and the heading before it, and note their levels (H2, H3…). This panel's Headings view lists them in order.
Read the section the heading starts, and decide whether it is part of the section above it (one level deeper) or a section of its own (the same level).
Check that its level is at most one deeper than the heading before it: after an H2 comes an H2 or an H3, not an H4.
The heading is at most one level deeper than the heading before it, so the outline has no gap.
The heading is more than one level deeper than the heading before it, so people who move from heading to heading miss a level. This is a best practice (G141), not a WCAG failure.
img_altQuality_review_TEXT_ALTERNATIVE_R: Find the image the report names and read its alternative text, in the image's settings.
Look at the image and the text around it, and ask what the image shows that matters to a reader.
For a chart or a diagram, the details can be in a caption or in the text next to it; the alternative text then only needs to say what it is.
Decide whether the alternative text says what matters. A file name, a web address or a word like "image" does not.
The alternative text says what the image shows that a reader needs, or says what it is while a caption or the text next to it gives the rest.
Nothing tells a reader who can't see the image what it shows (the alternative text is a file name, for example), which fails WCAG 1.1.1 (F30).
img_altDecorative_review_EXCLUDED_ELEMEN: Find the image the report names. It is marked as decorative (its alternative text is empty), so screen readers skip it.
Ask what a reader would miss if the image weren't there: information, a label, a chart's figures, or nothing.
If it shows something that matters, check whether the text next to it already says the same.
The image is only decoration, or the text next to it already says what it shows, so skipping it loses nothing.
The image shows something nothing else on the page says, but screen readers skip it, which fails WCAG 1.1.1. Give it alternative text.
linkNameQualityLinkOnly_review_GENERIC_L: Find the link the report names, "{{name|the link}}", and read its text on its own, without the sentence around it.
Decide whether that text alone says where the link goes. Screen readers can list a page's links on their own, without the sentences around them.
If it doesn't, the link text can say where it goes: "the price list" rather than "click here".
The link text says where the link goes on its own.
Only the sentence around the link says where it goes, which fails WCAG 2.4.9 (AAA, F84).
linkNameQuality_review_GENERIC_LINK_TEXT: Find the link the report names, "{{name|the link}}", and read its text on its own, without the sentence around it.
Decide whether that text alone says where the link goes. Screen readers can list a page's links on their own, without the sentences around them.
If it doesn't, the link text can say where it goes: "the price list" rather than "click here".
The link text says where the link goes on its own.
Only the sentence around the link says where it goes, which fails WCAG 2.4.9 (AAA, F84).
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_SHORT_PARAGRAPH_s: Find the bold line the report names and read it together with the text after it.
Decide whether it is a title for that text, as "Opening hours" is above the hours, or emphasis that belongs to the text.
If it is a title, check in the editor whether it is a heading or a paragraph made bold.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_SHORT_PARAGRAPH_p: The bold line is emphasis, a label or a note that is part of the text, or it is already a heading.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_SHORT_PARAGRAPH_f: The bold line is a title for the text after it but is a paragraph made bold, so screen reader users can't find it among the headings, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F2). Make it a heading.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_LARGE_PARAGRAPH_s: Find the large bold text the report names and read it together with the text after it.
Decide whether it is a title for that text, or emphasis, a quotation, a price or a figure.
If it is a title, check in the editor whether it is a heading or a paragraph made large and bold.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_LARGE_PARAGRAPH_p: The text is not a title (it is emphasis, a quotation, a price or a figure), or it is already a heading.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_LARGE_PARAGRAPH_f: The text is a title for what follows but is a paragraph made large and bold, so screen reader users can't find it among the headings, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F2). Make it a heading.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_LINK_step: Find the large bold link the report names and read it together with the text after it.
Decide whether it is a title for that text, as a post's title in a list of posts is, or just a link.
If it is a title, check in the editor whether it is a heading with a link in it, or a paragraph with a large bold link.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_LINK_pass: The link is not a title, or it is already inside a heading.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_LINK_fail: The link is a title for what follows but is not a heading, so screen reader users can't find it among the headings, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F2). Put it in a heading.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_NUMBER_st: Find the large bold number the report names (a year, for example) and read it together with the text after it.
Decide whether it is a title for that text, as a year is above that year's events, or a figure, such as a price or a statistic.
If it is a title, check in the editor whether it is a heading or a paragraph made large and bold.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_NUMBER_pa: The number is a figure, not a title, or it is already a heading.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_NUMBER_fa: The number is a title for what follows but is a paragraph made large and bold, so screen reader users can't find it among the headings, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F2). Make it a heading.
tdHasHeader_review_TD_TABLE_NO_HEADERS_s: Look at the table the report names.
Decide whether it holds data in rows and columns, with a top row or first column that labels the rest, or only places content side by side.
If it holds data, check in the table's settings that its top row is set as a header row.
tdHasHeader_review_TD_TABLE_NO_HEADERS_p: The table only places content side by side, or its label row is set as a header row.
tdHasHeader_review_TD_TABLE_NO_HEADERS_f: The table holds data but has no header row, so screen reader users aren't told what each value means, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F46).
contrastComputable_review_BACKGROUND_IMA: Find the text the report names and look at the image or gradient behind it.
Find the part of the background behind the letters that is closest to the text's colour: the lightest part behind dark text, the darkest behind light text.
Compare the text's colour with it in a contrast checker: it needs 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text (24 pixels, or 19 pixels in bold).
If the image changes (on a narrow screen, or between slides), check each version.
Every part of the background behind the letters gives at least that ratio, for example thanks to a dark overlay behind light text.
Some part of the background behind the text is too close to its colour, below that ratio, which fails WCAG 1.4.3. A darker or lighter overlay, or a plain background behind the text, fixes it.
